C005.subject: Evolution-inspired AI architectures with explicit cooperation rewards that also incorporate inter-agent communication channels
C005.object: architectures without such communication in sustaining cooperative dynamics under individual fitness selection pressure
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Evolution-inspired AI architectures with explicit cooperation rewards that also incorporate inter-agent communication channels architectures without such communication in sustaining cooperative dynamics under individual fitness selection pressure]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled experiments in a cooperative foraging or resource-sharing environment (e.g., a modified version of the 'Apple Gathering' or 'Level-Based Foraging' domain) comparing communication-enabled vs. communication-free agents under individual selection pressure, with explicit cooperation rewards. — Direct empirical comparison in a well-understood multi-agent RL benchmark can isolate the effect of communication channels on sustaining cooperation, controlling for reward shaping and selection pressure.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis using evolutionary game theory or multi-agent reinforcement learning dynamics (e.g., replicator dynamics or Nash Q-learning) to model the impact of inter-agent communication on the stability of cooperative equilibria under individual fitness selection. — Formal modeling can predict whether communication channels fundamentally alter the conditions for cooperation collapse, providing a mechanism-level explanation that complements empirical findings.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of recent (2020-2023) studies on 'emergent communication' and 'cooperation in multi-agent systems' from venues such as AAMAS, NeurIPS, or ICLR, focusing on papers that explicitly test communication's effect on cooperative dynamics under individual rewards. — Synthesizing existing results can reveal whether the hypothesized advantage holds across diverse settings (e.g., discrete vs. continuous communication, different reward structures) and identify boundary conditions or contradictory findings.

scope.domain: multi-agent reinforcement learning with engineered reward shaping and communication constraints

qualifier.temporal: as of 2023 experimental results in simulated environments

C006.subject: Evolution-inspired AI architectures with explicit cooperation rewards
C006.object: cooperative and mutually beneficial dynamics due to overriding selection pressures for individual fitness
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Evolution-inspired AI architectures with explicit cooperation rewards cooperative and mutually beneficial dynamics due to overriding selection pressures for individual fitness]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled experiments comparing cooperative reward shaping vs. individual selection in MARL environments (e.g., Hanabi, Overcooked, or resource-collection grids) with explicit measurement of emergent cooperation and individual fitness trade-offs. — Directly tests whether explicit cooperation rewards can overcome individual selection pressures; published results often show breakdown under high individual reward variance.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of evolutionary game dynamics in multi-agent reinforcement learning, e.g., using replicator dynamics or Nash equilibrium analysis to model conditions under which cooperation rewards are stable against defection. — Provides formal predictions about when cooperation rewards fail due to selection for individual fitness, helping to confirm or refute the hypothesis mathematically.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of recent literature (2020–2025) on population-based training and coevolutionary algorithms in multi-agent systems, focusing on studies that report cooperation collapse despite engineered rewards. — Aggregates existing evidence to assess the generality of the failure pattern and identify boundary conditions, such as reward sparsity or agent heterogeneity.

scope.domain: multi-agent reinforcement learning with engineered reward shaping

qualifier.geographic: global academic and industrial AI research laboratories

C007.subject: Standard evolution-inspired AI architectures (e.g., NEAT, novelty search)
C007.object: sustained cooperative dynamics when individual fitness is augmented with a minimal spatial or temporal correlation constraint
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Standard evolution-inspired AI architectures (e.g., NEAT, novelty search) sustained cooperative dynamics when individual fitness is augmented with a minimal spatial or temporal correlation constraint]

[PATH:empirical] Re-run NEAT and novelty search in a grid-based spatial arena (e.g., 100x100 torus) with a minimal spatial correlation constraint (e.g., local resource sharing within a 3x3 neighborhood) and measure the rate of cooperation (e.g., proportion of cooperative acts or mutualistic strategies) over 10,000 generations, comparing against baselines without the constraint. — Directly tests the hypothesis under the specified temporal and geographic scope, providing quantitative evidence for or against sustained cooperative dynamics.

[PATH:literature] Survey and meta-analyze existing literature on spatial and temporal constraints in evolutionary AI (e.g., studies on spatially structured evolutionary games, temporal niche partitioning in NEAT, or cooperative behavior in novelty search with shared resources). — Evaluates whether prior results align with the hypothesis, identifying patterns across different architectures and environments to confirm or refute the claim without new experiments.

[PATH:theoretical] Develop a theoretical model of open-ended evolution with local interaction neighborhoods and a minimal temporal correlation constraint (e.g., periodic resource renewal or delayed fitness feedback), analyzing the stability of cooperative equilibria using replicator dynamics or evolutionary game theory. — Provides a formal framework to predict conditions under which cooperation emerges and persists, complementing empirical tests and clarifying the role of the constraint.

scope.domain: open-ended evolutionary optimization with local interaction neighborhoods or shared resource niches

qualifier.temporal: during the first 10,000 generations of evolution in simulated environments
qualifier.geographic: in virtual grid-based and continuous 2D spatial arenas

C008.subject: Standard evolution-inspired AI architectures (e.g., NEAT, novelty search)
C008.object: sustained cooperative dynamics under pure individual fitness selection
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Standard evolution-inspired AI architectures (e.g., NEAT, novelty search) sustained cooperative dynamics under pure individual fitness selection]

[PATH:empirical] Replicating the 'cooperative backbones' experiment from 'Evolution of Cooperation in Evolutionary Robotics' (e.g., Waibel et al., 2009) using NEAT with purely individual fitness, and measuring sustained cooperation over >10,000 generations — Directly tests whether NEAT can evolve cooperation without explicit group selection or reward sharing, providing a clear replication target for the hypothesis.

[PATH:literature] Systematic literature review of novelty search and NEAT studies that report emergent cooperative behaviors (e.g., in multi-agent foraging or social dilemma tasks), focusing on whether cooperation was sustained or collapsed after initial emergence — Aggregates existing evidence to assess whether the claimed effect is robust across different implementations and task domains, or whether it is an artifact of specific parameter settings.

[PATH:theoretical] Formal analysis of the evolutionary dynamics in minimal models (e.g., iterated prisoner's dilemma with NEAT-like mutation and selection) using Price's equation or replicator-mutator models, to derive conditions under which cooperative strategies can be fixed under individual fitness — Provides a mathematical foundation to predict whether and when sustained cooperation is possible, helping to refute or confirm the hypothesis beyond case-specific simulations.

scope.domain: open-ended evolutionary optimization without additional cooperative mechanisms

C011.subject: Evolution-inspired AI architectures that incorporate both indirect reciprocity and spatial structure
C011.object: high levels of cooperation even under strong individual selection pressure, by using a reputation-based partner selection mechanism that reinforces spatial clusters
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Evolution-inspired AI architectures that incorporate both indirect reciprocity and spatial structure high levels of cooperation even under strong individual selection pressure, by using a reputation-based partner selection mechanism that reinforces spatial clusters]

[PATH:empirical] Repeated public goods game experiments with spatial lattice structures and reputation scoring (e.g., using agent-based models similar to Nowak & Sigmund's indirect reciprocity framework but extended to 2D grids and partner choice) — Direct simulation can test whether adding a reputation-based partner selection mechanism to spatially structured populations (e.g., on a lattice or network) yields stable cooperation under high selection pressure, and whether spatial clusters indeed form and persist.

[PATH:theoretical] Analytical models of evolutionary dynamics combining indirect reciprocity with spatial viscosity (e.g., replicator dynamics or adaptive dynamics on graphs with image scoring) — Mathematical analysis can determine necessary conditions (e.g., benefit-to-cost ratio, mutation rate, network topology) for stable cooperation when reputation and space interact, providing a rigorous check on the hypothesized mechanism's robustness.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of existing literature on 'spatial indirect reciprocity' and 'partner selection in evolutionary games' (e.g., studies by Santos, Pacheco, or Sigmund on network reciprocity and reputation) — A systematic review of published results can reveal whether the combined effect has been previously observed or contradicted, and identify parameter regimes where the hypothesis holds or fails, thus confirming or refuting the claim without new experiments.

scope.domain: evolutionary game theory simulations with population structure

qualifier.mechanism: combined indirect reciprocity and spatial clustering with reputation-based partner selection
